newsitem.title: USA: NASD blunder purges regulatory broker data - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: NASD blunder purges regulatory broker data - WSJ.

text.p: A mistake by the National Association of Securities Dealers has caused as many as 20,000 pieces of regulatory data on the nation's stock brokers to be purged, the Wall Street Journal said Friday.
The paper, citing state regulators and others, said the information was purged from the computer system used to track disciplinary histories of stock brokers and their firms.
The report said NASD would confirm only that about 3,000 filed were purged, but said state regulators believe the number is 20,000.

The data includes those involving intances when a customer, court or arbitration panel withdraws or dismisses a complaint or dismisses a broker named in a lawsuit or arbitration filing, the report said.
The report quoted a NASD official as saying that the agency is in the process of restoring the records and expects to finish the task within 60 days.
